lesson_body:
Welcome back, young mathematicians! Today, we are diving deeper into the exciting world of counting as we explore different ways to think about numbers. In our last lesson, we learned that counting is not just about saying numbers aloud, but also about understanding how to group them and recognize patterns. Let's recall how we counted objects around us last time! Can you remember some of the items we counted together? Wonderful! Today, we're going to focus on counting in groups and using our fingers to help us.

We will start by introducing the concept of 'grouping.' Grouping means putting items together into smaller sets. For example, if we have 10 apples, we can group them into 2 sets of 5 apples each! This helps us see that counting can be easier and more fun. Let’s practice this by using some fun objects! Here is a set of colored blocks. How many blocks do we have? Let's count them together. Now, let's try to group them into sets of two. Can you do that? Count out loud as you make the groups. 

To make our counting even more enjoyable, we will have a celebration of number bonds! A number bond shows how two smaller numbers can make a bigger number. For instance, if we have 3 red blocks and 2 blue blocks, together they form a group of 5 blocks. Let’s draw some number bonds in our math journals. You can use stickers or crayons to illustrate your number bonds. This will help us visualize how numbers are connected!

Finally, before we wrap up, let’s play a counting game! You can choose your favorite toy or household item. Count how many you have, write it down, and see if you can create different groups with those items. Remember, counting is all about exploring and having fun. Tomorrow we will continue building on what we learned today, so keep practicing your counting and grouping at home, and we will see wonderful results!
interactive_assignment: Today’s interactive assignment is to create a 'Counting Collage!' You will need to gather various small objects from around your home, such as buttons, coins, or pieces of fruit. Once you have your collection, organize the objects into groups of 2, 3, or 5. After you’ve grouped them, take a picture of your arrangement. In your math journal, draw a picture of your collage and write down how many groups you made, how many objects are in each group, and what the total number is. Use stickers or crayons to decorate your journal page to make your counting collage colorful and fun!

daily_assessment.question: How many apples are in a group if we group 10 apples into sets of 5?
